exposure_registry.update_rule: Every later read of data in any v3 window, before the freeze, is appended here with its date and purpose. No quote, bar or official price at a v3 entry or exit stamp is fetched before the freeze: the 2017-2019 cost sample is the first step of the frozen evaluation (cost_model.out_of_period_spreads). Such a pre-freeze read is forbidden, not tolerated. If one happens anyway it is appended here and recorded as a numbered deviation before the freeze, and it voids development screening for the affected population (D or I): no item that uses that population can be nominated at development, so each such item scores p = 1 in the validation Holm run. A read of v3-defined outcomes in the validation window before the freeze voids validation; a read in the holdout window before the gate opens voids the holdout. The only permitted pre-freeze access is pre_freeze_access_path; data fetched and read only through it are not a read in this sense and do not void validation.

pre_freeze_access_path.rule: Before the freeze, 2016-2020 data (and the 2024-11-01 to 2025-12-31 covariate sessions of tercile_rule.holdout_breakpoints) are fetched only by committed count-only code. Raw pages go straight into a private snapshot sealed by sha256 and are never opened by a person or by any other code. The count-only code emits only counts and rates: no price, spread, return, gain, covariate value, event list or symbol-level row. Its committed output is the input to the freeze preconditions (coverage checks, corporate-action checks and the snapshot pin). The same sealed snapshot is the frozen evaluation's input for what it contains; everything else a stage needs is fetched after the freeze under run_discipline.fetch.
pre_freeze_access_path.snapshot_contents: (1) 2016-01-04 to 2020-12-31, the whole exchange-listed universe: daily bars raw, adjustment=split and adjustment=all; official prints with their sessions_io.official_price source labels; split, reverse-split and cash-dividend records; the coverage-stamp quotes of quote_coverage_stamps. No minute bar and no other quote for 2016-2020 is fetched before the freeze. (2) 2024-11-01 to 2025-12-31, the whole exchange-listed universe, for holdout breakpoints only: daily bars raw, adjustment=split and adjustment=all; official prints with their labels; corporate-action records; 1-minute SIP bars from 04:00 ET to the scheduled close (I membership needs 04:00-10:30, D's regular-session dollar volume needs 09:30 to the close); and, only if H5 is recorded as tested, FINRA consolidated short interest with its settlement and publication dates. No quote for 2024-11-01 to 2025-12-31 is fetched. Every part is pinned by sha256 with its fetch date as asof (freeze_preconditions).
pre_freeze_access_path.outputs: per calendar year and listing exchange: symbol-sessions with a daily bar, with a raw close >= $1, with each sessions_io.official_price source label for the open and the close (populations.official_prints), with split, reverse-split and cash-dividend records, and with a suspected unadjusted split (populations.suspected_unadjusted_split); coverage-stamp quote counts (quote_coverage_stamps); for 2024-11-01 to 2025-12-31 also symbol-sessions with at least one 1-minute bar before 10:30 ET and, if fetched, short-interest records per settlement date; for H2's gate (hypotheses.H2), identity and filing-index completeness counts over the coverage-stamp sample
pre_freeze_access_path.quote_coverage_stamps: Eligible-quote rates are measured only at stamps that are never v3 entry or exit stamps: 12:17 ET and 14:43 ET (12:17 and 12:43 ET on a 13:00 early close) on symbol-sessions selected by int.from_bytes(sha256('mover-v3-coverage|' + symbol + '|' + session)[:8], 'big') % 500 == 0 among all symbol-sessions with a daily bar and raw close >= $1, with no reference to event membership. A stamp has an eligible quote if the NBBO prevailing at the stamp is eligible (populations.fill_quote) and at most 1000 ms old, or if the first eligible quote update after the stamp arrives within 60 s. The code reports, per year, the stamps with an eligible quote (populations.halts), without one, and fetch-incomplete (populations.fetch_failures), and nothing else.
pre_freeze_access_path.runs: The count-only code runs once, from a committed revision named in its output. Every run, including a failed or partial one, is appended to this registry with its revision, date and output sha256. A rerun is allowed only after a failed or incomplete run, and never after its rates were read; the first complete run's output governs coverage_rule.
pre_freeze_access_path.not_allowed: no pre-freeze fetch or read of a quote at a D or I entry stamp, an exit stamp, or a cost-sample stamp; no opening of the sealed snapshot's bars or prints by a person or by code other than the count-only code; no computation of D or I membership, MAX21, DTC or any outcome

populations.D_daily: symbol-sessions t with split-consistent official-close gain close[t]/ref(t) - 1 >= 0.20 (close[t] is the accepted official close of populations.official_prints; a session without one is not an event and is counted, with no bar fallback; ref(t) as populations.formulas states), official close >= $1.00 and regular-session dollar volume DV_reg(t) >= $1,000,000 (populations.formulas); decision at 16:15 ET on t; entry at the first eligible quote at or after 09:35 ET on t+1 and at or after decision + 60 s; entry timeout 300 s, else no entry (counted)
populations.I_intraday: the first minute m in 09:35-10:30 ET on a session at which gain_at_m >= 0.20, dollar_volume_at_m >= $1,000,000 and price_at_m >= $1.00 (populations.formulas); entry at the first eligible quote at or after m + 60 s; timeout 60 s
populations.formulas: Restated exactly, so membership does not depend on unpinned code. f(t) = (raw close / split-adjusted close on the previous XNYS session) / (the same on t), from daily bars with adjustment=raw and adjustment=split, set to 1 when |f - 1| <= 1e-2 or any input is missing. This is rules.split_factor's arithmetic at aa6fc79 with adjustment=split closes in place of adjustment=all closes: with adjustment=all, a cash dividend of about 1% or more makes |f - 1| > 1e-2 on its ex-date, so rules.split_factor (and #162's D7 share_mult in evaluate_v2.py) books it as a share change; v3 departs from that deliberately. adjustment=all is used only for the cash remainder (populations.corporate_actions). ref(t) = the accepted official close of the previous XNYS session / f(t); if that session has no accepted official close, ref(t) is undefined and t is neither a D nor an I event (counted). There is no daily-bar or last-bar fallback (features.py and mover_scan.py at aa6fc79 fall back to the daily bar close; v3 does not). For minute m on session t: (price_at_m, dollar_volume_at_m) = rules.Bars.state(epoch of m ET) at aa6fc79, the close of the last 1-minute SIP bar starting before m and the summed vwap x volume of the session's bars from 04:00 ET starting before m; gain_at_m = price_at_m / ref(t) - 1, compared with 0.20 - 1e-9. DV_reg(t) = the summed vwap x volume of the 1-minute SIP bars of session t starting at or after 09:30 ET and before the scheduled close (session_calendar); a session with no such bar has DV_reg 0. Split-consistent official-close return of session j: r(j) = C(j) x f(j) / C(j-1) - 1, where C is the accepted official close (official_prints); r(j) is undefined if either close is missing. MAX21(t) = max over k = 1..21 of r(t-k), that is the 21 returns of sessions t-21 .. t-1 from the 22 accepted official closes of sessions t-22 .. t-1, for D and I alike (a D event's own session t is not in its window). If any of those 22 closes is missing, or any session t-21 .. t-1 is a suspected unadjusted split, MAX21 is undefined and the event is unassigned for H1 (counted, tercile_rule.minimum treatment); there is no maximum over fewer returns. Sizing window W(t) = the 20 sessions ending at t for D (its close is known at the 16:15 decision) and ending at t-1 for I. med20 = the median of DV_reg over W(t); sigma_d = the sample standard deviation (ddof = 1) of log(1 + r(j)) over the 20 sessions j of W(t). If any DV_reg or r(j) in W(t) is undefined, the trade cannot be sized and is a counted no-fill (cost_model.fix_2_impact_and_capacity). Entry bar = the last 1-minute SIP bar of the entry session (from 04:00 ET) that is complete at the fill-decision time X (it starts at or before X - 60 s); if there is none, the entry-bar cap is 0 and the trade is a counted no-fill. A synthetic test fixes each formula, including a split day, a missing previous close, a missing close inside the MAX21 window, a suspected unadjusted split inside it, a D versus I sizing window and an entry with no completed bar.
populations.official_prints: Accepted source labels of sessions_io.official_price at aa6fc79 (listing exchange = the exchange of the largest condition-O opening print; no O print means no listing exchange for that session). Official open: opening_print_listing_exchange only. Official close: closing_print_listing_exchange or official_close_listing_exchange only. closing_print_other_exchange, and a session with no O print, count as no official close and are counted per year. The same rule applies to close[t], to ref(t)'s previous close, to every H3-c leg and to H4 closing-cross folds. The synthetic suite has one case per source label, including the rejected label and a session with a closing print but no opening print.
populations.suspected_unadjusted_split: Applied before membership. For session t, r = raw daily close[t] / raw daily close[previous XNYS session]. If f(t) = 1 (no split adjustment in the adjustment=split bars, populations.formulas) and |r - n| <= 0.01 x n or |r - 1/n| <= 0.01 / n for some integer n in 2..100, t is a suspected unadjusted split: it is not a D or I event, any trade whose hold spans t (entry session through exit session) is excluded, and any event whose MAX21 window contains t is unassigned for H1 (tercile_rule.minimum treatment). All three are counted per stage. This also removes genuine moves within 1% of an integer multiple (for example +100%); that loss is preregistered and counted, not corrected.
populations.fetch_failures: Every quote request is retried up to 3 times with exponential backoff (1 s, 4 s, 16 s). A stamp whose pages are still incomplete (quotes.py stamp_incomplete, or any HTTP error) is fetch-incomplete: the trade that needs it is excluded, not counted as a no-entry or a delayed exit, and the count is reported per item. If more than 1% of the stamps a stage requires are fetch-incomplete after the single re-fetch of run_discipline.fetch, that stage is void: every item scores p = 1 and is labelled underpowered there, with the reason stated. The rate is committed before any outcome of the stage, and a void is final once that re-fetch is done; there is no further fetch attempt.
populations.session_calendar: XNYS from exchange_calendars 4.13.2 (the version rules.py C26 used for 2021-2026), for 2016-01-01 through the end of the last possible holdout extension. The session list, with each session's scheduled open and close, is written to a v3-owned file (blueprints/us-equities/mover-v3/session-calendar.json) and pinned by sha256 at the freeze. A 'full NYSE session' or 'session' anywhere in this protocol is every scheduled XNYS trading session, early closes included; no session count excludes early closes. Synthetic tests use the 2017-07-03, 2017-11-24, 2018-11-23, 2019-12-24 and 2020-11-27 early closes. Amendment: the pinned file cannot know unscheduled future closures (for example a national day of mourning). Such a closure is removed from the calendar by an append-only amendment that cites its primary source (NYSE notice) and is logged in the holdout access log before the next session. The session of the freeze and N0 keep the dates computed at the freeze from the pinned file, and if N0's date itself closes, the holdout starts at the next session. The 252-session holdout and each 63-session block count actual sessions, so their end dates move later by one session per removed closure. A synthetic test covers a removed session inside the holdout.
populations.session_times: Every '15:55 ET' in this protocol means the scheduled close (session_calendar) minus 5 minutes (12:55 ET on a 13:00 early-close session). Eligible quotes are regular-session quotes, at or after 09:30 ET and before the scheduled close. An exit that finds no eligible quote before the scheduled close takes the first eligible quote of the next session. D decisions stay at 16:15 ET on early-close sessions.
populations.fill_quote: For a fill at or after time X, the quote is the NBBO prevailing at X (the latest quote update stamped at or before X) if it is eligible and X minus its timestamp is at most 1000 ms; otherwise the first eligible quote update stamped after X, with fill time equal to its timestamp. Quote age is the fill-decision time minus the quote timestamp. Eligible: bid > 0 and ask > bid (locked and crossed quotes excluded), regular session (session_times). The same eligibility applies to fills and to cost-table cells (quotes.py valid_quote at aa6fc79 excludes locked and crossed quotes). Timeouts run from X. Synthetic tests cover a fresh prevailing quote, a stale one, a locked one and no quote inside the timeout.
populations.fill_price: Every entry and exit fills at the mid (bid + ask) / 2 of the eligible quote that fills it, so gross returns are mid-to-mid and cost_model adds the per-side cost on top. The realized half-spread of each fill quote is recorded and reported as a sensitivity (cost = 1.25 x max(table hs', realized half-spread)).
populations.corporate_actions: For every multi-session arm (D b_lane, H3 b_overnight, the H4 parents) and each H3-c leg, deviation D7's method is restated: the exit uses the raw exit mid (or raw official print for H3-c); shares change by the product of the split factors f(j) of populations.formulas (from adjustment=split bars, a factor counting when it differs from 1 by more than 1e-2) over the sessions after the entry session through the exit session; the rest of the adjustment=all close-to-close return over the hold is booked as cash per original share, without spread or fees. This departs from D7 as implemented in evaluate_v2.py at aa6fc79, whose share_mult comes from adjustment=all closes and so counts a cash dividend of about 1% or more as a share change. Fees use the actual exit shares and raw exit price. H3-c legs use log((raw end print x split factor + cash) / raw start print). H5's short interest and 20-session volume are both expressed in session t's share basis with the same split factors. Study code must pass synthetic tests before the freeze that cross a split, an ordinary ex-dividend date and a special cash dividend of 5% (booked as cash with f = 1, never as a share change, and not flagged as a suspected unadjusted split).
populations.exclusions: (1) Not exchange-listed on the session: a symbol-session is eligible only if it has a listing exchange under populations.official_prints (an exchange's condition-O opening print on that session), so OTC-only trading is excluded by as-known session data; the current Alpaca asset exchange and tradable flags (used by mover_scan.py at aa6fc79) are never used, being look-ahead and survivorship-prone for 2016-2020. (2) Warrants, units and rights, by this literal rule (candidates.py at aa6fc79; mover_scan.py's DERIV = ^[A-Z]{4}[WUR]$|\.(WS|U|R|W) is the same set): exclude the symbol if (len(symbol) == 5 and re.search('[A-Z]{4}[WUR]$', symbol)) or re.search('\.(WS|U|R|W)', symbol) (Python re, unanchored search), and, as mover_scan.py also does, any symbol containing '/'. (3) Symbols with fewer than 21 prior XNYS sessions with a daily bar. Each exclusion is counted per stage, with a synthetic test per rule. No halt exclusion: H1-H3 use no halt data (see halts).
populations.halts: H1-H3 use no halt source, historically or prospectively, so their trade sets cannot depend on a later data purchase. As in catalyst-experiment, a halt is never inferred from missing data: an entry or exit fills only at an eligible quote (populations.fill_quote), an entry without one inside its timeout is a counted no-entry, and an exit without one waits for the next eligible quote. Limitation: a trade that sits through an unobserved halt is not flagged, and a fill at the first post-halt quote is not distinguished from a normal fill. Halt state enters only H4, as an overlay on already-defined trades.
populations.parameter_provenance: G = 0.20 and V = $1M are v1's loosest gain and middle volume floor, fixed for sample size after v1's all-negative dev/val grid was seen (disclosed exposure). They are not tuned on any v3 window.

coverage_rule.scope: Every D- and I-based item, that is all of H1-H5 (H2, H4 and H5 use the same D and I trades, 2016-2020 quotes and official closes, and H4's parents are the H1/H2/H5 b_lane trades), with one set of kept years per stage shared by every item. H2, H4 and H5 also need their own data gates. Decided at the freeze from the count-only outputs (exposure_registry.pre_freeze_access_path), before any outcome, and recorded beside multiple_testing.data_status_at_freeze.
coverage_rule.no_fallback: A session or symbol without an accepted official print or an eligible quote stays a counted non-event, no-entry or excluded trade under its own rule; no bar, quote or other-exchange substitute is ever used.
coverage_rule.year_rule: A calendar year of 2016-2020 whose accepted official-close rate (symbol-sessions with an accepted official close / symbol-sessions with a daily bar and raw close >= $1) is below 90%, or whose eligible-quote rate at the coverage stamps is below 80%, is dropped from its stage entirely (every session of that year; for 2016, the warm-up, events of early 2017 then stay unassigned under tercile_rule.minimum until 60 prior events accrue). The thresholds are design choices, not measured values.
coverage_rule.item_rule: If fewer than 2 development years remain, or 2020 is dropped, no item of H1-H5 is tested: all 35 items score p = 1 at every stage, permanently, and that is the recorded result of this protocol version. The same year rule applies to D and I alike.
coverage_rule.dropped_year_consequences: (a) Breakpoints: a dropped year's sessions are skipped, as holdout_breakpoints skips its gap; the trailing window of tercile_rule is the 252 most recent kept sessions strictly before s, and a dropped year's events never enter it. (b) Segments: each edge of a dropped year is a segment boundary under chronology.boundaries, so a trade entered before a dropped year whose planned exit falls inside it is censored on the last kept session before it, no trade enters in the dropped year, and multi-session arms give up the first 6 kept sessions after it as entry sessions. (c) Bootstrap: the stage's kept sessions are concatenated in date order and the circular block bootstrap wraps over that kept list. Each has a synthetic test with a dropped middle year.
coverage_rule.limitation: The coverage stamps sample the whole $1+ universe, not movers; mover quote coverage may be lower. Per-stage no-entry and excluded counts are reported so that this is visible.

tercile_rule.breakpoints: For a covariate X (MAX21 in H1, DTC in H5) and a population P, the breakpoints for an event decided in session s are the 1/3 and 2/3 empirical quantiles (numpy 'linear' method) of X over all P events with a defined X whose decision session lies in the 252 kept sessions strictly before s (coverage_rule.dropped_year_consequences). Every P event counts, whether it entered, had no entry or had no fill. Every input is known at the decision, including for I, whose later same-morning triggers are never used.
tercile_rule.holdout_breakpoints: For a holdout event the trailing window is the 252 most recent sessions before s that lie outside 2026-01-02 to session N0 - 1. That gap covers #162's reserved holdout (2026-01-02 to 2026-09-18, which v3 never reads) and every session from 2026-09-21 to N0 - 1, whose events never enter a breakpoint window (the sessions from the freeze session to N0 - 1 are collected only as lookback inputs, holdout_gate.prospective_collection). The window therefore draws only on (a) the 252 sessions ending 2025-12-31 (v1/v2 validation, already exposed), whose covariates and event membership come from the pre-freeze sealed snapshot (pre_freeze_access_path.snapshot_contents part 2: daily bars, official prints, corporate actions, 1-minute bars from 04:00 ET to the close and, if H5 is tested, FINRA short interest, from 2024-11-01 for the MAX21, ref and 20-session lookbacks to 2025-12-31, asof its fetch date) and are computed only after the gate opens; and (b) earlier holdout sessions, from the sealed holdout snapshot's decision-time inputs, read only after the gate opens. It reads only covariates and event membership, never an outcome. A synthetic test computes the breakpoints for the first holdout session from part (a) alone.
tercile_rule.assignment: low if X <= the 1/3 breakpoint, high if X > the 2/3 breakpoint, middle otherwise (a value equal to a breakpoint goes to the lower tercile)
tercile_rule.h5_event_set: For H5, P is the set of D events with a defined DTC (a FINRA figure published before the decision). D events without DTC are counted and reported per stage but are not H5 events: they are outside the H5 breakpoint set, the 60-event minimum and every H5 cell.
tercile_rule.minimum: if fewer than 60 prior P events lie in the trailing window, the event is unassigned: it is counted and reported, and it enters no tercile cell or difference test. The 2016 warm-up year supplies the first window.
tercile_rule.small_dates: Terciles never depend on the number of movers on the event's own date, so a date with fewer than 3 movers needs no special rule.

holdout.window: 252 sessions (session_calendar) starting at session N0 = the 40th session after the session of the freeze. N0 is fixed by the freeze commit alone. The freeze commit is the first commit reachable from origin/main (first-parent history) in which this file's status is frozen; this repository squash-merges pull requests, so a commit that exists only on a PR branch is never the freeze commit. Its committer timestamp, converted to America/New_York, is the freeze time, and the session of the freeze is the first XNYS session (session_calendar) whose scheduled open is at or after the freeze time. D decisions made on session N0 - 1 enter on N0 and belong to the holdout (chronology.boundaries assigns by entry session). Development and validation run by committed automation started at the freeze, and the commit that adds the validation results file (with its sha256 in the run log, run_discipline) must be reachable from origin/main before 09:30 ET on session N0, measured by the GitHub-recorded time it became reachable (the pull request's merged_at, or the push event for a direct push), which the run log records. If it is not, the holdout of this protocol version is void for every item, whatever the reason; a new protocol version is required. There is no deferral, so the start cannot be chosen after the validation results or the live market are seen.
holdout.extension: if any carried item has fewer than its minimum holdout trades after 252 sessions, extend in 63-session blocks, at most 2. The holdout window is common to every carried item: once extended, every carried item is evaluated over the extended window. A carried item still below its minimum after the second block is labelled underpowered. Each extension decision uses one 'count' read (holdout_gate.access_log) whose unit is count_unit, never an exit or outcome price
holdout.count_unit: For each carried item, the number of trades that would enter that item's statistic at the read: events that pass membership and every exclusion, have an entry fill quote inside the entry timeout, have filled notional >= $1,000, are not fetch-incomplete, hold no suspected unadjusted split, have an assigned tercile, catalyst group or halted-parent status where the item needs one, and have every exit quote or official print the item needs present (for H3-c, all 8 official legs). Only presence and exclusion flags are evaluated: no price, mid, spread, return or exit value is computed or emitted. The same unit applies to the minimum_sample checks. A synthetic test asserts that the count output carries only integers keyed by item_ids and that the count code path calls no price or return function.
holdout.why_prospective: No retrospective window free of prior mover outcomes remains: 2021-2025 is v1/v2 dev/val, 2026-01-02 to 2026-09-18 is #162's reserved holdout and is event-level exposed, 2017-2026-08-14 is broad-universe exposed at aggregate level, and 2016 is warm-up.
holdout.accrual_exposure: The primary holdout statistic of every item uses every holdout trade; nothing is excluded for exposure. Paper exposure is recorded only for symbol-sessions in which a paper order was submitted, logged at order time (symbol, session, order id, strategy) in the collection batch's accrual log before any outcome of that trade exists. A holdout D trade is paper-exposed if any session in [decision t, planned exit] is such a symbol-session; an I trade if its event session is. The result without paper-exposed trades is reported only as a sensitivity. If the paper-exposed fraction of any carried item's holdout trades exceeds 5%, the holdout is labelled contaminated for that item, which can then not be labelled supported (confirmatory). A holdout read never excludes a trade; a read without a granted entry voids the holdout for every item (holdout_gate.access_log.rule). The engineering protocol's positions follow its population rule and are logged the same way.
holdout.holdout_read: A holdout read is exactly this: computing, from data of sessions N0 onward, any v3-defined outcome, meaning a price at a v3 exit stamp paired with a v3 entry, or a forward return, net return or leg return of a v3 D or I event (populations, hypotheses), or any statistic built from one. Only such a computation inside a granted 'read' entry is permitted; a 'count' entry permits count_unit only. Not a read: (1) collection under holdout_gate.prospective_collection, including computing the collected batch's sha256; (2) live paper decisions and orders of any strategy, including the NautilusTrader paper runs and their decision streams, which are exposure and are logged in the accrual log; (3) dashboards and timers that publish metadata only (counts, liveness, freshness), such as the grand-dashboard checkpoint; (4) computing D or I membership without any outcome, when done by committed code whose output is logged in the accrual log (for example a paper strategy's own screen). A synthetic test classifies one example of each case.

labels.development: disjoint from v1/v2; exposed at aggregate level through broad-universe development (both lanes, 2017-2021); screening only; survivorship-limited before 2020 (names delisted in 2016-2019 without a retained corporate action cannot be discovered)
labels.validation: disjoint from v1/v2; exposed at aggregate level through broad-universe development (both lanes include 2020) and the S2 headline the author read; screening only, never confirmatory; the 2020 COVID regime is reported separately and never dropped
labels.holdout: prospective; untouched only if the validation results commit was reachable from origin/main before 09:30 ET on N0, no holdout read (chronology.holdout.holdout_read) preceded a committed granted access-log entry, every collection batch has its committed accrual log, and no carried item's paper-exposed fraction exceeds 5% (accrual_exposure)

chronology.boundaries: Segments are assigned by entry session. A trade whose planned exit falls after its segment's last session is censored: it exits at the first eligible quote at or after 15:55 ET on that last session, is flagged, stays in the earlier segment's means and is reported as a count. H3 b_overnight makes no entry on a segment's last session (counted), and an H3-c trade whose legs cross the segment end is excluded from H3-c and counted. For multi-session arms, the later segment gives up its first 6 sessions as entry sessions (an embargo after the censored crossing trades); same-session arms need no gap.

labels.passes_stage: the item passes its stage rule, with a stage-specific name: 'nominated' at development (the screen), 'screened' at validation (Holm in the 35-item family plus minimum sample and, for a tradable cell, the robustness means), 'supported (confirmatory)' at the holdout (the same at the holdout). Only the holdout label is a claim.
labels.not_supported_mde_excluded: the stage has at least its minimum sample, the item does not pass, and the one-sided bootstrap-percentile confidence bound (from the same B draws, numpy 'linear' quantile) at Bonferroni level a = 0.05/35 excludes an effect of the preregistered MDE for the realized n (minimum_detectable_effect, with the item's sigma from minimum_detectable_effect.sigma_by_item). For an alternative 'less than 0' the bound is the lower bound, the a-quantile of the bootstrap statistics, and the MDE is excluded when it is greater than -MDE. For an alternative 'greater than 0' (every tradable cell, and H3-c or H4 locked positive) the bound is the upper bound, the (1 - a)-quantile, and the MDE is excluded when it is less than +MDE. For H3-c and H4 at development, where no direction is locked yet, a = 0.05/70 and both hold: the lower bound is greater than -MDE and the upper bound is less than +MDE. The fixed Bonferroni level is used because Holm's step-down level is not defined for items after the first retained hypothesis.
labels.underpowered: the stage is below its minimum sample, or the item neither passes nor excludes the MDE

outcome_reporting.hypothesis_verdict: A hypothesis-level verdict (each not_supported_if) is computed at validation, reported as a screening verdict, and, for a hypothesis with a carried item, at the holdout, reported as the confirmatory verdict. Each uses the labels of its own stage only: 'no tradable cell passes' means no tradable cell of that hypothesis passes that stage.
outcome_reporting.validation_reporting: Every item's validation estimate, interval and label are computed and reported descriptively, whether or not development nominated it; only nominated items receive a Holm p, and the rest score p = 1 in the Holm run.
outcome_reporting.qualifiers: Contamination and lineage status are qualifiers attached to a label, never labels of their own. A holdout item that meets the holdout pass rule while its holdout is contaminated (chronology.holdout.accrual_exposure) is labelled 'screened (contaminated holdout)', the screening-level pass name, and never 'supported (confirmatory)'. An item labelled 'supported (confirmatory)' that is not lineage-confirmed (multiple_testing.lineage_sensitivity) carries the qualifier 'lineage-unconfirmed'. A stage decided by a post-deviation rerun (run_discipline.deviations) carries 'post-deviation'.
outcome_reporting.rule: Only these three labels are used, with the qualifiers above. A miss is never reported as 'falsified' or as proof of no effect; 'not supported' always states the size it excludes. A result in the direction opposite to a one-sided alternative is reported descriptively with its estimate and interval and supports no claim, because it was not tested.

H1.name: MAX/lottery conditioning of mover outcomes

evidence.source: Bali, Cakici, Whitelaw (2011) JFE 99(2), https://pages.stern.nyu.edu/~rwhitela/papers/max%20jfe.pdf; NBER w14804
catalyst-experiment/protocol.json ranks by relative_volume then price_return, a MAX-like selection

H1.covariate: MAX21 as populations.formulas defines it: the largest of the 21 split-consistent accepted-official-close returns of sessions t-21 .. t-1, for D and I alike, undefined (event unassigned, counted) if any of the 22 closes is missing or a suspected unadjusted split lies in the window; terciles by tercile_rule (trailing 252-session breakpoints of the same population)

exit_arms.a_fast: first eligible quote at or after min(entry + 30 min, 15:55 ET)
exit_arms.b_lane: D: first eligible quote at or after 15:55 ET on the 5th holding session (entry session = 1); I: at or after min(entry + 60 min, 15:55)
exit_arms.c_session: first eligible quote at or after 15:55 ET on the entry session

H1.stops: none beyond the engine margin rule

primary_tests.statistic: mean net(b_lane | high MAX tercile) - mean net(b_lane | low MAX tercile), population D

H1.tradable_cells: 2 populations x 3 arms x 3 terciles = 18; each tested for mean net > 0
H1.not_supported_if: at the verdict stage (outcome_reporting.hypothesis_verdict), H1-D and H1-I are both labelled not_supported_mde_excluded and no H1 tradable cell passes. A high-MAX outperformance is outside the one-sided alternative, is reported descriptively only, and supports no claim about the reversal prior.
H1.data_status: expected available (Alpaca SIP daily and minute bars, quotes and official prices), but conditional: historical quote and auction-print coverage for 2016-2020 is unverified, and H1 is tested only if coverage_rule keeps enough years (multiple_testing.data_status_at_freeze)

H2.name: Catalyst-verified movers versus pure attention spikes

evidence.source: Barber & Odean (2008) RFS 21(2); Barber, Huang, Odean, Schwarz (2022) JF doi 10.1111/jofi.13183; Barber, Lin, Odean (2023) JFQA
evidence.status: contested: refutation concerned a citation and the fit, not the direction; used as a prior on retail P&L only

H2.split: catalyst: an 8-K with Item 1.01 whose EDGAR acceptance time precedes the decision and falls after the previous regular close (D) or in [the regular open of session t-3, decision minute m) (I); attention: the symbol's as-known CIK has a complete, parsed filing index for that window with no qualifying filing. A symbol with no as-known CIK, an incomplete index or an unparsed filing is 'identity/item unknown', reported apart and excluded from both groups; absence of a filing is never inferred from silence.

primary_tests.statistic: mean net(catalyst) - mean net(attention), population D

H2.not_supported_if: at the verdict stage (outcome_reporting.hypothesis_verdict), H2-D and H2-I are both labelled not_supported_mde_excluded and no H2 tradable cell passes: the catalyst filter adds nothing beyond the volume filter at the detectable size.
H2.data_status: gated: cannot be computed with the repository's code as it stands. catalyst.py sets available_at = max(acceptance, local first observation), so every 2016-2020 filing observed in 2026 fails historical eligibility; it has no Item 1.01 parser and no historical ticker-to-CIK map. Before the freeze H2 needs (1) a preregistered historical availability rule, EDGAR acceptance time taken as original availability with that limitation stated, which departs from the catalyst-experiment rule and must be recorded as such; (2) a committed Item parser (for example from the header's ITEM INFORMATION lines) with synthetic tests; (3) a dated as-known ticker-to-CIK source; (4) a metadata coverage check of identity and filing-index completeness over a population that uses no membership: the coverage-stamp sample of exposure_registry.pre_freeze_access_path.quote_coverage_stamps (1 in 500 symbol-sessions with a daily bar and raw close >= $1, 2016-2020), run by the count-only code, since D and I membership may not be computed before the freeze; mover completeness may be lower, and per-stage 'identity/item unknown' counts make that visible; (5) the prospective commitment of multiple_testing.prospective_data. If any is missing at the freeze, H2 is recorded as not tested (multiple_testing.data_status_at_freeze).

H3.name: Overnight versus intraday legs of mover holds

evidence.source: Lou, Polk, Skouras (2019) 'A tug of war: Overnight versus intraday expected returns', JFE 134(1):192-213, doi 10.1016/j.jfineco.2019.03.011; Akbas, Boehmer, Jiang, Koch (2022) 'Overnight returns, daytime reversals, and future stock returns', JFE 145(3):850-875, doi 10.1016/j.jfineco.2021.09.019
evidence.status: contested: the original citation was a secondary summary; substance not refuted; both DOIs resolved in Crossref metadata on 2026-09-24, full texts not read; large, liquid names

evidence.source: Maroy, SSRN 5095349 (posted 2025-01-12), VWAP and ladder exits
evidence.status: contested: HTTP 403, not read; excluded from the confirmatory family

H3.price_sources: official open and official close as populations.official_prints accepts them (sessions_io.official_price at aa6fc79, accepted labels only; closing_print_other_exchange counts as missing). A trade with any missing official print among its 8 legs is excluded from H3-c and counted; no bar or quote substitutes in H3-c, and no trade is averaged over fewer legs.

exit_arms.a_intraday: enter at the first eligible quote at or after 09:35 on t+1, timeout 300 s as for D, else no entry (counted); exit at or after 15:55 the same session. H3-a's trades are the H1 D c_session trades pooled across terciles, plus unassigned events; the overlap is intended and is reported, and H3-a keeps its own Holm slot.
exit_arms.b_overnight: enter at the first eligible quote at or after 15:55 on t+1, timeout 300 s, else no entry (counted); exit at the first eligible quote at or after 09:30 on t+2
exit_arms.c_decomposition: diagnostic only, not traded: over the sessions t+1 .. t+5 of the D b_lane hold, overnight legs k = 1..4 are official close of t+k to official open of t+k+1, and intraday legs k = 2..5 are official open to official close of t+k. The partial first-session leg is excluded, so each trade has 4 legs of each kind, and together they decompose official close(t+1) to official close(t+5).

H3.sizing: 1x; arm b stays at 1x in any later paper use until leverage-ladder-2x and its overnight cap are clean

primary_tests.statistic: mean over trades of (mean of the 4 overnight leg log returns - mean of the 4 intraday leg log returns), gross, legs as in c_decomposition
primary_tests.alternative: not equal to 0 at development; after development, one-sided in the direction of the development estimate (multiple_testing.direction_lock)
primary_tests.minimum_sample: one-sample paired statistic: the tradable_cell minima apply to trades with all 8 legs

H3.tradable_cells: H3-a and H3-b are the tradable cells (counted once)
H3.not_supported_if: at the verdict stage (outcome_reporting.hypothesis_verdict), H3-c is labelled not_supported_mde_excluded and neither H3-a nor H3-b passes after costs.
H3.data_status: expected available (Alpaca SIP minute bars and quotes; official opening and closing auction prints), but conditional: 2016-2020 quote and auction-print coverage is unverified, and H3 is tested only if coverage_rule keeps enough years (multiple_testing.data_status_at_freeze)

H4.name: Halt-conditional exit around LULD pauses and halts

evidence.source: SEC DERA LULD white papers, https://www.sec.gov/files/dera-luld-white-paper.pdf and https://www.sec.gov/files/marketstructure/research/dera_wp_luld_and_extraordinary_transitory_volatility.pdf
evidence.status: contested: the execution-state idea survives; the pause-duration claim is a literature-review statement, not a DERA finding

evidence.source: Nasdaq 'All About LULDs' and the NasdaqTrader LULD FAQ (15 s limit state, 5-minute pause, last-10-minute pauses fold into the close)
evidence.status: contested: opened by the reviewer; band tiers must be checked against the current plan text before any hardcoding

evidence.source: Nasdaq TotalView-ITCH 5.0 specification (NQTVITCHSpecification.pdf) section 1.2.2 Stock Trading Action: coverage is 'all exchange-listed equities securities traded via the Nasdaq execution system'; state H is 'Halted across all U.S. equity markets / SROs'; P (paused) is 'Nasdaq-listed securities only', and 'Trading pauses on non-NASDAQ listed securities will be treated simply as a halt'; the J LULD Auction Collar applies to a paused security reopening
evidence.status: read on 2026-09-24 in the review fix round; the Databento XNAS.ITCH status schema that carries it is contested (sweep p1-databento-xnas-itch-halt-luld) and its cost and coverage start are unverified

H4.parent_trades: the b_lane trades of populations D and I (the trades H1, H2 and H5 share), deduplicated by symbol|entry session|entry timestamp. Other arms (H1 a_fast and c_session, H3 a and b) are not parents. The unit of analysis and of the session block bootstrap is one deduplicated parent trade.
H4.population: every parent trade whose security enters state H (halted across all US markets) or, for a Nasdaq-listed security, P (LULD pause), per the covered halt source, at a time after the entry fill and before the planned b_lane exit. A halt already in force at the entry stamp delays or prevents the entry (populations.fill_quote) and does not make the parent halted. The two strata are reported separately: an LULD pause is identified only for Nasdaq-listed names; for other listings the source reports a pause as a halt.

exit_arms.a_reopen: exit at the reopening of the first halt or pause that starts after the entry fill (later halts in the same hold are ignored by a_reopen and logged), at the primary listing's reopening-cross print, else the mid of the first eligible post-reopen quote. The print source is fixed before the freeze by metadata (for example XNAS.ITCH cross-trade messages for Nasdaq listings, or SIP trade conditions that mark the reopening cross); the Databento status schema carries no trades. Without a fixed print source, a_reopen uses the first eligible post-reopen quote only.
exit_arms.b_ignore: hold to the parent b_lane exit, ignoring the halt

H4.edge_cases: (1) A halt that is still in force at the planned b_lane exit: both arms exit at the same first eligible post-reopen price, so the pair difference is 0; the case stays in the sample and is counted. (2) A halt still in force at the end of the segment's last session (chronology.boundaries): the parent is excluded from H4 and counted. (3) A pause in the last 10 minutes that folds into the closing cross: the reopening is the closing cross, so a_reopen exits at the accepted official close (populations.official_prints), else the first eligible quote of the next session. (4) Several halts in one hold: a_reopen uses the first; b_ignore holds through all of them. Each case has a synthetic test.
H4.rules: No fills during a halt; a resting stop fills through the gap at the first print. Pause duration is logged as a covariate only. Both arms' sides are costed at 1.25 x max(table hs', the realized half-spread of the fill quote, or of the first eligible post-reopen quote for a cross print), because post-reopen spreads on halted movers are wider than the table's time-bucket cells. Bootstrap blocks are 10 sessions for all H4 parents.

primary_tests.statistic: mean over halted parent trades of net(a_reopen) - net(b_ignore) (paired, one-sample)
primary_tests.alternative: not equal to 0 at development; after development, one-sided in the direction of the development estimate (multiple_testing.direction_lock)

H4.not_supported_if: at the verdict stage (outcome_reporting.hypothesis_verdict), H4 is labelled not_supported_mde_excluded. A stage below its minimum halted trades is underpowered, not a miss; either way the halt state stays a safety rule only.
H4.data_status: gated: Databento XNAS.ITCH status schema (paid, metered; covers halt and resume state for every security traded on the Nasdaq execution system, with the P pause state and J auction collar for Nasdaq-listed securities only; cost and coverage start unverified; *contested*), or Nasdaq Trader halt history (free, limited lookback, pilot only). Whether SIP conditions can rebuild halts is unverified.
H4.chronology: common, restricted to the halt source's covered sessions as established by metadata before any outcome. A Nasdaq Trader pilot is exploratory and cannot pass. If the covered development span is shorter than 1 year, or the data are not in hand at the freeze, or no prospective_data entry covers its holdout (multiple_testing.prospective_data), H4 is not tested and scores p = 1 at every stage, permanently (multiple_testing.data_status_at_freeze). The halt source is used only for H4 and never changes the H1-H3 trade sets.

evidence.source: Hong, Li, Ni, Scheinkman, Yan, 'Days to Cover and Stock Returns', NBER w21166, SSRN 10.2139/ssrn.2568768
evidence.status: survives: high DTC predicts lower returns. The paper makes no squeeze claim.

evidence.source: S3 Partners crowding and short-squeeze paper, EFMA 2025 conference draft (http://www.efmaefm.org/0EFMAMEETINGS/EFMA%20ANNUAL%20MEETINGS/2025-Greece/papers/Manuscript-with-author-details223.pdf)
evidence.status: unverified conference draft, not confirmed as published; the sweep's only source for 'squeezes are episodic, not a base rate'. Not a prior for H5-s.

evidence.source: blueprints/us-equities/acceptance-wave/factors-regimes.md: FINRA consolidatedShortInterest is not a realtime squeeze signal

H5.covariate: DTC = the most recent FINRA short interest published before the decision (publication and settlement lag respected) / 20-session median share volume ending t, both in session t's share basis (populations.corporate_actions); terciles by tercile_rule over the H5 event set (tercile_rule.h5_event_set: D events with a defined DTC; D events without one are counted and reported but are not H5 events)
H5.sizing: 1x; the overlay filters and never sizes

primary_tests.statistic: mean net(high DTC) - mean net(low DTC)
mean net(high DTC) - mean net(middle and low DTC pooled); unequal groups, so its MDE uses sqrt(1/n1 + 1/n2)
primary_tests.prior: none sourced: Hong et al. point the other way (H5-p) and the squeeze base-rate statement rests on an unverified draft. H5-s is a secondary test with no directional prior and is expected to be not supported.

H5.not_supported_if: at the verdict stage (outcome_reporting.hypothesis_verdict), H5-p (or H5-s, reported separately) is labelled not_supported_mde_excluded and no H5 tradable cell passes.
H5.data_status: gated on FINRA short-interest access and terms, which the user must establish; bi-monthly, an overlay only
H5.chronology: common, restricted to sessions whose decision has a published figure. Published history must cover the 2016 warm-up (tercile_rule needs 60 prior D events), at least 1 development year and the whole validation year. If it does not, or the data are not in hand at the freeze, or no prospective_data entry covers its holdout (multiple_testing.prospective_data), H5 is not tested and both tests score p = 1 at every stage, permanently (multiple_testing.data_status_at_freeze).

H6.name: Execution parity: broker-held exits versus client-side exits (engineering, not alpha)
H6.status: gated in its own draft: it has no position source yet, and its call-count test was restated as descriptive because the client-side arm needs fewer calls by construction
H6.why: H6 accrues on a live paper timeline unrelated to the 2020 validation window or the 252-session holdout, and its equivalence test needs larger stages than this family's. It is its own engineering protocol with its own one-test family; it uses no slot of the alpha family, H1-H5 never wait for it, and its result never opens this protocol's holdout.

multiple_testing.family: one family across H1-H5: the 8 non-tradable primary tests (H1-D, H1-I, H2-D, H2-I, H3-c, H4, H5-p, H5-s) plus the 27 tradable cells (H1 18, H2 4, H3 2, H5 3), m = 35. H6 is not in this family.
multiple_testing.item_id_rule: Tradable cell ids are hypothesis-population-arm-group (H3-a and H3-b are both primary tests and tradable cells). item_ids is the complete list, in bytewise ASCII order, which is the order used for stream spawning, for the final tie-break and for the validation results file.
multiple_testing.procedure: Holm step-down at family-wise alpha 0.05, applied separately at validation and at the holdout. An item not carried to a stage, or not tested for lack of data, scores p = 1 there. The validation results file, when committed, contains all 35 validation p-values keyed by item_ids (1 for items not carried or not tested); an incomplete file is refused by the evaluator.
multiple_testing.direction_lock: H3-c and H4 are two-sided only at development: the development screen uses the two-sided p = 2 x min(one-sided p), and the sign of the development estimate is recorded in the development results file. Validation and the holdout then use the one-sided test in that recorded direction, in the same Holm slot. A significant result in the opposite direction at validation or the holdout is reported descriptively and cannot pass.
multiple_testing.data_status_at_freeze: At the freeze each of H1 and H3 (coverage_rule) and each of H2, H4 and H5 is recorded as either 'data in hand, tested' or 'not tested, p = 1 at every stage, permanently'. Data from a new source, or a new historical range, acquired after the freeze can support only a new protocol version with its own family; it never enters this family's Holm run, so a late small p cannot loosen other items' thresholds. The prospective holdout data of a tested item under its committed prospective_data entry are not new data in this sense.
multiple_testing.prospective_data: At the freeze, each tested item whose holdout needs data beyond the Alpaca SIP collection (H2: EDGAR filings and the ticker-to-CIK source; H4: the halt source and reopening-print source; H5: FINRA short interest) records a committed prospective source, licence and budget covering the full holdout plus both 63-session extension blocks; an item without one is recorded as not tested. The purchase or collection follows that record whatever validation shows. A carried item whose holdout data do not arrive, in full or in part, is labelled underpowered at the holdout with the reason stated, and is never dropped silently or replaced.
multiple_testing.development_screen: unadjusted p <= 0.05 with the minimum sample: one-sided in the stated direction for directional items, two-sided for H3-c and H4 (direction_lock); development only nominates items for validation
multiple_testing.lineage_sensitivity: The mover question has already tried 1,012 rule-exits (v1 768, v2 244) and broad-universe-mover-v1's 60 predeclared signal variants (5 signals x 3 horizons x 2 selections x 2 instrument lanes) on overlapping or other windows. Every validation and holdout p is also reported against Bonferroni 0.05 / (1012 + 60 + 35) = 4.52e-5. broad-universe's 2 controls and its descriptive lane are not counted: they are base-rate reports with no pass rule (its promotion 'never'); that exclusion is a stated limitation. Each p is reported beside a normal-tail p from the same bootstrap standard error. With B = 100,000 a bootstrap p at 4.52e-5 means at most 3 null-side draws, so the bootstrap p alone cannot resolve this level (its Monte Carlo error is about the size of the threshold). An item is lineage-confirmed only if both its bootstrap p and its normal-tail p are at or below 4.52e-5; an item that passes Holm but not both keeps its stage label with the qualifier 'lineage-unconfirmed' (outcome_reporting.qualifiers).
multiple_testing.tie_breaks: Where items tie on a p (for example at the floor 1 / (B + 1)), in the holdout cap of 5 tradable cells or in Holm ordering, ties are broken by the normal-tail p, then by item id in bytewise ASCII order (item_ids).
multiple_testing.tests_not_in_family: BH (q = 0.10) diagnostics across tercile, year, price-tier and halt-covariate splits are reported but can never open the holdout

minimum_sample.one_sample_paired: H3-c uses the tradable_cell minima (trades with all 8 legs); H4 uses its minimum_halted_trades
minimum_sample.rule: A stage below its minimum reports the item as underpowered (outcome_reporting); it cannot pass that stage. Minima are counted in chronology.holdout.count_unit (trades that enter the item's statistic after every exclusion), at every stage.

minimum_detectable_effect.formula: MDE = (z_alpha + z(0.80)) x sigma x sqrt(DEFF) x sqrt(1/n) for one cell or a one-sample paired statistic (H3-c, H4); x sqrt(1/n1 + 1/n2) in place of sqrt(1/n) for a two-group difference (so sqrt(2/n) for equal groups; realized trailing terciles are not exactly 1/3 each, and H5-s pools two terciles). z_alpha = z(1 - 0.05/35) = 2.983 for one-sided tests, including H3-c and H4 after development (direction_lock), and z(1 - 0.05/70) = 3.189 for H3-c and H4 at development. The MDE is computed from the planning sigma below and the realized n; it is never re-estimated from outcomes.

sigma_by_item.rule: Each of the 35 item_ids takes the sigma of its arm and the MDE form of its statistic: 'cell' uses sqrt(1/n), 'difference' uses sqrt(1/n1 + 1/n2), 'paired' is a one-sample paired statistic with sqrt(1/n). I b_lane (min(entry + 60 min, 15:55)) is a 30-to-60-minute arm; D b_lane is a 5-session arm; H3-a (09:35 to 15:55) is a same-session close arm.

minimum_detectable_effect.sigma_provenance: 0.10 and 0.25 are (P95 - P5) / 3.29 from #162 v1 development aggregates (07:00|G0.20|V1000000 X2 and X1: P5 -15.0% / P95 +18.0%, and P5 -42.1% / P95 +39.5%); normal approximation, which understates fat tails. Those rule-exits entered at 07:00 ET in the pre-market, so their spread for 09:35 entries is not measured. 0.35, 0.15 (one 15:55-to-09:30 leg), 0.10 (the difference of two 4-leg means of log returns) and 0.35 for H4 (dominated by the remaining b_ignore path) are assumptions with no measured source. DEFF 1.5 for session clustering is an assumption.
minimum_detectable_effect.table_note: The two-sided table applies only to H3-c (sigma 0.10) and H4 (sigma 0.35) at development; both are one-sample paired statistics. The earlier two-group two-sided table was misapplied and is removed. n40 and n60 are H4's validation/holdout and development minima.
minimum_detectable_effect.reading: Only large effects can pass or be excluded. The literature's effects (about 1% a month for MAX and days to cover) are far below these MDEs, so a miss on H1-D, H1-I or H5 will most likely be labelled underpowered, and v3 is informative only about large mover-specific effects.

lookup.cell_key: time_bucket|price_tier|dv_tier, per side, from that side's fill: time bucket of the fill timestamp, price tier of the fill price, and dv tier of the session's cumulative dollar volume at the fill timestamp (rules.py Bars.cum_dv, the summed vwap x volume of bars starting before the timestamp; the same input v1 evaluate.py passes as entry_cum_dv and exit_cum_dv). For a D entry at 09:35 this is t+1's cumulative dollar volume at 09:35; for a 5-session exit it is the exit session's cumulative dollar volume at the exit timestamp.

fix_1_monotone_dollar_volume.finding: #162 review item costs-F1: cells under $1M dollar volume fall back to a time x price pool that costs about half the $1-5M cell (for example 3|2|0 0.24% vs 3|2|1 0.75%)
fix_1_monotone_dollar_volume.rule: for each time x price bucket, hs'(>= $5M) = hs(>= $5M); hs'($1-5M) = max(hs($1-5M), hs'(>= $5M)); hs'(< $1M) = max(hs(< $1M), hs'($1-5M)). A less liquid tier is never cheaper than a more liquid one. Applied last, after out_of_period_spreads.
fix_1_monotone_dollar_volume.note: the before/after values are for the base table alone; the final values follow the 2017-2019 re-measure.

fix_2_impact_and_capacity.finding: #162 review item costs-F4: pass statistics use a fixed $20k notional with no impact term and assume full fills
fix_2_impact_and_capacity.notional: filled notional = min($20,000; 1% of med20; 10% of the entry bar's dollar volume, vwap x volume), with med20 and the entry bar (the last 1-minute bar complete at the fill-decision time, so it never includes volume after the fill) as populations.formulas defines them. No auction volume is used: every fill is at a quote mid (populations.fill_price). The excess is not filled. A trade with filled notional under $1,000, or one that cannot be sized, is a no-fill and is counted.
fix_2_impact_and_capacity.impact: impact per side (return) = c x sigma_d x sqrt(q), where q = filled notional / med20 and sigma_d is populations.formulas' standard deviation of split-consistent official-close log returns over the sizing window W(t), both known at the decision. Primary c = 1.0; sensitivities c = 0.5 and 2.0.
fix_2_impact_and_capacity.provenance: The square-root functional form and the c grid are design choices bracketing the unknown; the sweep supplies no source for them.

out_of_period_spreads.sample: The first step of the frozen evaluation, after the freeze and before any other outcome: 1 in 20 development (2017-2019) D and I entries is selected by quotes.py's sample_key at aa6fc79: int.from_bytes(sha256('symbol|session|hhmm')[:8], 'big') % 20 == 0, with the v3 entry's symbol, entry session and entry HH:MM ET. Each selected entry is stamped at its entry timestamp, entry + 15 min, entry + 60 min and 5 minutes before that session's scheduled close from session_calendar (the v1 stamp set; quotes.py cmd_sample's stamping is not reused, because rules.close_hhmm misses 2016-2020 early closes). Those stamps coincide with D c_session and I b_lane exits, so they are outcome prices; measuring them before the freeze would expose development outcomes, which #162 v1 avoided by freezing first. The sampling rule, the table method and the combine rule are fixed here, so no value is chosen after the sample is seen.
out_of_period_spreads.table: cells are built with quotes.py's table method at aa6fc79, including the D7 stamp-window guard and v1's sparse-cell fallbacks: a cell with >= 30 observations (MIN_CELL) uses its trimmed mean, else the time x price pool if it has >= 30, else the table's 90th percentile
out_of_period_spreads.combine: each cell's cost is max(hs from the base table, hs from the 2017-2019 table); fix_1 is then applied to the result

cost_model.per_side: 1.25 x hs' + impact, for continuous and auction sides alike (v1's 0.5x auction discount is not reused); H4 sides use the halt-specific rule in hypotheses.H4.rules
cost_model.fees: a v3-owned file, blueprints/us-equities/mover-v3/fees-v3.json, pinned by sha256 at the freeze. It carries SEC Section 31 and FINRA TAF rows in force from 2017-01-01 through the holdout, each with its primary source and quote; #162 fees.json at aa6fc79 (sha256 fa1f468b80f78dc0c050948123116f577e38ae9f8c03f9fb360d11042a3fed3d) is left unchanged and is not used, because its SEC rows start at 2020-01-01 for lookup convenience only. Rates announced after the freeze for holdout dates are appended from primary sources before the holdout read, logged in the access log, and never change an earlier row. v3 code computes fees from this file, not from rules.sell_fees. Alpaca commission 0; IBKR tiered as a broker variant. A synthetic test looks up a 2017 and a 2019 sale.
cost_model.break_even: the cost multiple at which each cell's mean net return reaches 0 is reported

statistics.estimator: trade-level mean net return; also median, 1%-winsorised mean, mean without the top 5 sessions and mean of per-session means
statistics.bootstrap: circular session block bootstrap, B = 100,000, over the stage's kept sessions concatenated in date order (coverage_rule.dropped_year_consequences); block length 5 sessions for same-session arms and 10 sessions for multi-session arms and for H4 (whose parents mix both); difference tests resample sessions jointly for both groups; generator numpy.random.Generator(PCG64), seeded per stage: stage_index 0 development, 1 validation, 2 holdout; each stage uses numpy.random.SeedSequence(entropy = the first 8 bytes of sha256(frozen protocol id) read big-endian, spawn_key = (stage_index,)).spawn(35), and child i drives item_ids[i] (multiple_testing.item_ids order), so no stage reuses another stage's stream
statistics.p_value: one-sided p = (1 + #{b : stat_b on the null side of 0}) / (B + 1); two-sided p = min(1, 2 x the smaller one-sided p)
statistics.robustness_required_for_a_pass: a tradable cell's validation and holdout passes also need a positive winsorised mean, mean without the top 5 sessions and mean of per-session means
sensitivities: without split-day rows (v3 has no fallback-price rows: populations.formulas and official_prints)
validation restricted to symbol-sessions that were not a broad-universe lane decision (exposure_registry.consequence)
cost from the realized half-spread of each fill quote (populations.fill_price)

holdout_gate.opens_only_for: items that passed validation: a primary test or tradable cell with Holm-adjusted validation p <= 0.05 in the 35-item family, the minimum validation sample and, for a tradable cell, the robustness means. At most 5 tradable cells, ranked by raw (unadjusted) validation bootstrap p with multiple_testing.tie_breaks, and every validated primary test.
holdout_gate.h4_scope: a validated H4 authorizes computing, in the holdout, the a_reopen and b_ignore exits of halted parent trades only (H4 parent_trades), whether or not any parent cell validated. It authorizes no non-halted parent outcome and no tradable-cell statistic.
holdout_gate.no_pass: If nothing validates, the holdout is never labelled or read, and that is the result.
holdout_gate.prospective_collection: Collected forward from the session of the freeze (chronology.holdout.window) by the frozen collector, so that the first holdout sessions have their 22-session MAX21, 20-session sizing and ref lookbacks and D decisions on N0 - 1 have their inputs. Each collection batch holds, for the whole exchange-listed universe and only these decision-time inputs: daily bars raw, adjustment=split and adjustment=all; 1-minute SIP bars from 04:00 ET to the scheduled close; official prints with their sessions_io.official_price labels; corporate-action records. Batches are sealed into a private snapshot whose sha256 is committed per batch with its accrual log. Quotes are not collected forward and nothing selects symbols by membership: the entry, exit and fill quotes of holdout trades, and any H2, H4 or H5 source a carried item needs (multiple_testing.prospective_data), are fetched only under a granted 'count' or 'read' access-log entry, by the frozen fetch code (run_discipline.fetch), with the fetch date as asof, and sealed before use. Sessions from the freeze to N0 - 1 serve only as lookback inputs. No outcome label, forward return or exit is computed from any batch before a granted 'read' entry. The collector and its synthetic tests (including a first-holdout-session test that needs the pre-N0 lookback) are freeze preconditions.

access_log.mode: append-only JSON lines, committed and pushed before the read it authorizes

purposes.collect: a collection batch, rows_read 0, listing that batch's accrual exposure
purposes.count: one at the end of the 252 sessions and one at the end of each extension block: chronology.holdout.count_unit per carried item, never an exit or outcome price; it may fetch the quotes and sources it needs under run_discipline.fetch; used only for the extension decision
purposes.read: the single outcome read for carried items

access_log.rule: Any holdout read without a preceding committed granted entry of the matching purpose voids the holdout for every item. Refusals are logged too. The 'count' path is tested in the synthetic suite, including a test that it computes no exit price.

run_discipline.study_code: The frozen protocol records study_code = {revision: the git commit of the study code, tree: the git tree hash of blueprints/us-equities/mover-v3/study/ at that commit}, plus the sha256 of the collector and fetch code it contains. Every run, fetch and evaluator call names the revision and tree it ran from, and the evaluator refuses to run from any other tree unless run_discipline.deviations allows it.
run_discipline.run_log: blueprints/us-equities/mover-v3/run-log.jsonl, append-only JSON lines. Every run of the frozen automation (cost sample, each stage's fetch and re-fetch, development, validation, each holdout 'count' and 'read'), including failed and partial runs, gets one line with utc start and end, stage, purpose, study_code revision and tree, input snapshot sha256s, status (complete, failed or partial), the sha256 of every results file it wrote (partial files included) and, for the validation results commit, the GitHub-recorded time it became reachable from origin/main. Each line is committed and pushed before the next run of any stage starts.
run_discipline.once: Development is computed by one logged run and validation by one logged run. The first run of a stage that writes any outcome is that stage's governing run, whether or not it completes: the governing development run nominates, and the governing validation run's results file governs the holdout gate.
run_discipline.deviations: Any change to the study code, the fetch code or a stage's inputs after the first outcome of any stage is a numbered deviation in blueprints/us-equities/mover-v3/deviations.json (cause, diff reference, affected stages), committed and pushed before any rerun. A rerun under a deviation is reported beside the governing run and never replaces it, with one exception: if the governing run is incomplete because of an exception or an infrastructure failure, one rerun under a deviation that changes no rule may govern, labelled 'post-deviation', provided it reproduces byte for byte every outcome the incomplete run had written; otherwise that stage is decided by the incomplete run's written outcomes alone if it is development (unwritten items score p = 1), and the holdout of this protocol version is void if it is validation. A deviation committed after any validation outcome exists never changes which items the holdout gate opens for.
run_discipline.fetch: Before any outcome of a stage (development, validation, the cost sample, and each holdout 'count' or 'read'), the frozen automation fetches every quote window, minute bar and official print that stage needs, deriving stamps only from decision-time inputs and quote timestamps, seals the result as a sha256-pinned private snapshot and commits that sha256 and the stage's fetch-incomplete rate (populations.fetch_failures) in the run log. At most one re-fetch is allowed, preregistered here: once, of only the fetch-incomplete stamps, before any outcome of that stage; its sealed result and new rate are committed the same way. After it the 1% void rule is final. Development and validation data fetched after the freeze are used only through these sealed snapshots, and no outcome is computed from unsealed data.
run_discipline.synthetic_tests: the evaluator refuses a results file from an unpinned revision or tree, a stage with a second outcome-bearing run that no deviation covers, and an outcome computed before the stage's fetch rate is committed

leverage_and_exits: Research runs use 1x equal notional. Paper use of any passing rule follows the README's exit and leverage policy: at most one broker-held closing order per share (a trailing_stop or an OCO per quantity tranche, as the Alpaca docs require), the leverage-schedule-v1-20260922 ceiling, and the leverage-ladder-1x/2x/4x gate rows in catalogs/us-equities/gates-20260922.json, one rung at a time with automatic step-down.
